messages:
Sam: FYI — ACME opened an urgent ticket: p99 spikes in their Dedicated pool during their monthly billing window. They see attach latencies up to 17s and intermittent 502s. Escalated to support.

Maria: Can you drop the ticket link + a sample trace? Need repro and whether it's strictly during billing window.

Sam: Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4521

Sam: sample attach log:
```
[2026-03-17T17:12:10Z] attach_request tenant=acme request_id=abc123 pool=dedicated-acme
[2026-03-17T17:12:11Z] queue_pos=42 provisioning_state=waiting
[2026-03-17T17:12:26Z] attach_error code=timeout detail="cold gpu attach took 15.2s"
[2026-03-17T17:12:26Z] response 502
```

Kyle: I pulled prometheus; provisioning_queue_length and attach_lat_p99 spike together. Looks like scale-up lag + cold GPU bootstrap under a sudden fanout.

Jess (eng-sre): Run the PromQL I use so we have numbers (queue tail + attach p99) for dedicated-acme across the window.

Sam: Run:
```
sum(rate(provisioning_queue_length{pool="dedicated-acme"}[1m])) by (pool)
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(attach_duration_seconds_bucket{pool="dedicated-acme"}[5m])) by (le))
```

Sam: Output pasted to ticket — queue went from ~2 -> 60 in ~90s; attach p99 ~16s.

Anya: Customer confirms this is every month at 17:00 UTC when their billing pipeline bursts parallel attaches.

Maria: Short-term mitigations we can offer now? Need low-friction fixes.

Kyle: Options:
- bump min_pool_size for their reserved pool during billing window
- enable proactive warmup (image pre-pull + model cache init) for that pool
- fallback routing to a smaller model variant that boots faster (if acceptable)
- throttle their route at API layer to smooth attach fanout

Jess (eng-sre): Autoscaler currently target_utilization=0.65 and min_pool=1 for this tenant. With sudden fanout scheduler serializes GPU attach which causes head-of-line delay.

Maria: Can ops bump min_pool now? Suggested value?

Sam: Recommend min_pool=4 for next 2 hours + prewarm=true. Should absorb the ramp and reduce p99 to ~500-800ms for warm attaches.

Ops Bot: Deploy request acknowledged — creating runbook entry and temporary policy.

Ops: Applied temporary config to dedicated-acme:
```
{ "tenant": "acme", "min_pool": "4", "prewarm": "true", "override_expires": "2026-03-17T19:30:00Z" }
```

Incidents Bot: Policy applied in 46s. Observability: provisioning_queue_length dropping, attach p99 trending down.

Sam: Customer reports improvement within 3 minutes — p99 down to ~650ms and 502s stopped. Billing job completed.

Anya: Good. We'll propose scheduled prewarm for their monthly billing window or increasing reserved baseline.

Jess (eng-sre): Follow-ups for engineering:
- investigate scheduler fairness: why attach ops serialized instead of parallel warm-attach path
- instrument cold GPU bootstrap (image pull, model cache init) and add telemetry
- evaluate fast-boot model variants for heavy-burst tenants

Kyle: Repro plan: run load test simulating 120 concurrent attaches over 2 minutes against a small dedicated pool (min_pool=1) and capture attach service logs + queue metrics. I'll run this in staging tomorrow.

Maria: Action owners: Kyle -> staging repro + dashboards; Jess -> scheduler deep-dive; Sam -> support playbook docs; Anya -> customer follow-up and proposal.

Sam: Thanks all — closing ticket after customer OK. I'll attach temp policy JSON and before/after graphs to SUP-4521.

Anya: Runbook note: when seeing attach p99 > 3s + queue length > 10 for dedicated tenant => suggest bump min_pool + enable prewarm before escalation.

Maria: 👍 please timestamp and put runbook snippet in shared KB.

Sam: Done — KB: https://docs.redwood.ai/support/runbooks/assignments#prewarm-dedicated-burst

Jess (eng-sre): Longer-term: consider calendar-based pre-warm (customer-defined windows) and a burst-credits mechanism to accelerate scale-up for predictable spikes.

Ops Bot: Note: temp policy expired at 2026-03-17T19:30:00Z per override; no further actions taken.

Kyle: Will run repro at 09:00 PT tomorrow and ping channel with logs.

Maria: Thanks everyone, quick mitigation worked. Closing thread when SUP-4521 updated with artifacts.
